questions.stem: Haemoglobin contains which metal as a central atom?
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin has four haem groups, each with an Fe²⁺ atom that reversibly binds O₂. (Chlorophyll — Mg; insulin — Zn-coordinated; haemocyanin of molluscs — Cu.)

questions.stem: The number of chromosomes in a normal human somatic cell is:
questions.explanation: 46 chromosomes (23 pairs, diploid). Gametes (sperm, egg) have 23 (haploid). Down syndrome = trisomy 21 (3 copies of chr 21 → 47 total).

questions.stem: Consider the following deficiency-disease pairings. Which is INCORRECTLY paired?
questions.explanation: Beri-beri is due to Vitamin B1 (thiamine) deficiency, NOT Vitamin D. Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets (in children) and osteomalacia (in adults). Other three pairs are correct.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about PHOTOSYNTHESIS. 1. The light-dependent reactions take place in the thylakoid membranes. 2. The Calvin cycle (light-INdependent) takes place in the stroma. 3. Water is the source of electrons (H) and the oxygen released during photosynthesis. 4. Chlorophyll-a is the primary pigment; accessory pigments include chlorophyll-b and carotenoids. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: All four correct. Light reactions — thylakoid grana. Calvin cycle — stroma. Water split via photolysis (2H2O → 4H⁺ + 4e⁻ + O2) — oxygen released. Chl-a absorbs ~430, 660 nm; Chl-b broadens the absorption; carotenoids (β-carotene, xanthophylls) absorb in blue region and protect against photo-oxidation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a VECTOR-borne disease?
questions.explanation: Leprosy (Mycobacterium leprae) is transmitted directly (droplet, close contact), NOT via a vector. Malaria (Anopheles mosquito), Dengue (Aedes aegypti), Kala-azar/Leishmaniasis (sand fly) ARE vector-borne.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Match the organ/gland with the HORMONE it primarily secretes. A. Pancreas (β-cells). B. Pituitary (posterior). C. Adrenal medulla. D. Thyroid. List-II: 1. Thyroxine (T4). 2. Adrenaline (epinephrine). 3. Insulin. 4. Oxytocin.
questions.explanation: β-cells of pancreatic islets — insulin. Posterior pituitary — stores and releases oxytocin + vasopressin (ADH). Adrenal medulla — adrenaline + noradrenaline. Thyroid — T4 (thyroxine) + T3 (tri-iodothyronine).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The LARGEST gland in the human body is the:
questions.explanation: Liver — ~1.5 kg in an adult, and the largest INTERNAL organ + largest gland. Performs bile secretion (exocrine) + many endocrine-like functions (regulates blood sugar via glycogen, produces IGF-1, etc.).
